source.title: LLM Unlearning Reveals a Stronger-Than-Expected Coreset Effect in Current Benchmarks
source.authors: Soumyadeep Pal; Chang-Sheng Wang; James Diffenderfer; B. Kailkhura; Si-Jia Liu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether attacks recover targeted knowledge after unlearning, using enhanced-GCG prompting and downstream fine-tuning. These are different from the claim’s cited examples but address the same recovery question.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports many coreset-size and selection-method results, but those compare unlearning efficacy across forget-set sizes rather than measure recovery from the attacks in the claim. Those results are not recorded here. Cited attack findings from other work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper's main subject is the coreset effect. Section 5 runs its own recovery attacks on WMDP-unlearned Zephyr-7B-β: enhanced-GCG prompts on RMU models (Table 3) and benign fine-tuning on GSM8k/AGNews for NPO models (Fig. 5). These results bear on whether unlearning resists recovery (A), on recovery by unrelated fine-tuning (B) and on recovery by jailbreak prompting (E).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that a 5% (even random) coreset achieves unlearning comparable to the full forget set, driven by keywords. They report that coreset-unlearned models suffer GCG-induced UE drops similar to full-set models, though they frame this as 'comparable robustness' rather than as recovery. Downstream fine-tuning causes relearning, and smaller coresets may be more vulnerable to it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard RMU and NPO unlearning, with forget-set coreset variants, then tests enhanced-GCG attacks and downstream fine-tuning; does not test gradient ascent or Who's Harry Potter.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning speed and extent vary by fine-tuning dataset, WMDP target, and forget-set ratio; the authors specifically note a distinction between coreset and full-set unlearning for WMDP-Bio with GSM8k.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning on WMDP and MUSE with RMU/NPO is matched using random 5% (RMU even 1%) coresets. Keyword-only forget sets capture most of the UE gain, which suggests current unlearning is driven by a few high-impact tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark unlearning success reflects suppression cued by a few keywords rather than removal of broad knowledge.

record.problems: Recovery tests use one model family and the reported fine-tuning results are figure-only, without exact values in the text. No matched model that never learned the targeted knowledge is reported for the recovery attacks, so the claim's stated no-more-than-never-learned comparison cannot be evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 also plots fine-tuning counts 32, 64, and 400 for each target, dataset, and forget-set ratio. These intermediate points are omitted to stay within the row budget; the figure's overall trend and the 8- and 600-sample endpoints are retained.

untested.parts: General ability (MMLU) is reported only for the unlearned models, not for attacked or fine-tuned checkpoints. GCG is tested only on RMU/WMDP-Bio, and fine-tuning only on NPO.
Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts or on loosely related data is not tested; only unrelated GSM8k/AGNews is used. RMU models are not fine-tuned.
Only enhanced-GCG is tested; rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not. No GCG test on NPO or WMDP-Cyber.

missing.what: Numeric UE readings from Fig. 5 at each fine-tuning count (including 32/64/400), against pre-unlearning UE (Bio 35.35, Cyber 55.51), to size the relearning.
Pre-unlearning UE baseline (35.35 for WMDP-Bio), needed to express GCG recovery as a fraction of what was removed.

record.verdict_notes: UE = 100 − WMDP accuracy; 75 equals chance. The authors present the recovery results as faithfulness checks on coresets, but the absolute numbers show substantial recovery from full-set RMU too. There is only one model family for the attacks. GCG uses RMU and fine-tuning uses NPO, so the two attacks are never applied to the same method.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures WMDP unlearning before and after an enhanced-GCG attack, but does not report a matched model that never learned the targeted knowledge or a general-ability measure for the attacked checkpoints.
Fine-tunes on GSM8k and AGNews examples, not on a subset of forgotten facts; the paper does not give exact numerical recovery values in the text.
No activation-direction ablation or direct test of access-blocking versus deletion.
Tests enhanced-GCG jailbreak prompts, but not rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
No newer counter-method is tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

rows.operation_detail: Applied enhanced-GCG adversarial prompt-prefix attack to an RMU-unlearned model.
rows.uncertainty: not stated
rows.note: The paper says a lower UE after attack indicates more successful recovery; the reported UE reduction is 21.75.
rows.check: State 'partial' is right for E. UE = 100 − accuracy, and pre-unlearning UE is 35.35 (Table 1). Accuracy goes from 30.5% after unlearning to 52.3% after attack, against 64.7% originally, so about 64% of the removed accuracy returns. For A, whose effect is 'no recovery', this row contradicts it. The baseline should also note the pre-unlearning UE of 35.35.

relation.reason: The paper runs its own recovery attacks and reports the results, though it frames them as a robustness check on coreset unlearning.

tranche.reason: Enhanced GCG on RMU models and benign fine-tuning of NPO models are different methods aimed at the original question. The paper's main subject is the coreset effect.

source_check.notes: Recovered shares: full set about 64%, 10% coreset about 51%, 5% about 57%. The '56–64%' in l3 and two statements should read 51–64%. All attacks use RANDOM coresets (10%: 10 epochs, 5%: 20 epochs, Table B2) on the authors' own runs. Fig. 5 panels are labelled (a),(b),(d),(e). The authors read the GCG result as 'comparable robustness' between coreset and full-set models.

statements.correction: If added: on the authors' own RMU Zephyr-7B-β (full forget set), enhanced GCG lowers WMDP-Bio UE from 69.46 to 47.71, i.e. accuracy goes from about 30.5% to 52.3% (Table 3).
statements.problem: The statement cites r1 but gives no number or claim for this study, so nothing about it is wrong. A reader can't see what r1 adds.

statements.correction: Share of removed accuracy recovered, with pre-unlearning UE 35.35 (Table 1): full set about 64%, 10% coreset about 51%, 5% coreset about 57%. The range is 51–64%. Coresets are RANDOM.
statements.problem: The UE values (69.46→47.71, 72.43→53.39, 72.03→51.29) are right. The derived 'roughly 56–64%' recovery is wrong for the 10% coreset.

statements.correction: Enhanced-GCG prefixes restore about 51–64% of the removed WMDP-Bio accuracy on RMU Zephyr-7B-β: 64% for the full set, 51% for the 10% coreset and 57% for the 5% coreset (Table 3, baseline UE 35.35).
statements.problem: 'Roughly 56–64%' is wrong for the 10% coreset, which restores about 51%.
The only figure given for this study is UE 69.46→47.71 (RMU Zephyr-7B-β, full forget set, enhanced GCG), and it is right.
